[PREFERENCE] User is excited to see their herbs grow.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Fresh herbs can elevate any salad to a whole new level!  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Consistent watering is essential for healthy herb growth.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips to keep fresh herbs fresh:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Store them properly: Rinse with cold water, pat dry, and store in a sealed container or plastic bag in the refrigerator.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Keep them cool: Store in the refrigerator at 32°F to 40°F (0°C to 4°C).  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Monitor moisture: Check daily and remove wilted or brown leaves.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Trim and prune: Regular trimming encourages bushy growth and prevents flowering.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Use the right storage container: Use a container with good air circulation.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 6. Freeze them: Chop and store in an airtight container or ice cube tray in the freezer.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 7. Harvest in the morning: Best time for flavor and aroma.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 8. Use the right herbs for the job: Basil, cilantro, parsley, dill, and mint are recommended for salads.  
[PREFERENCE] User will keep the tips in mind.  
[FACT] User has been using a balanced fertilizer for their cherry tomato plants.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in trying something more natural and cost-effective for fertilization.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Homemade fertilizers can reduce costs and create a sustainable gardening practice.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Recipes for homemade fertilizers:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Epsom Salt Fertilizer: Mix 1 tablespoon of Epsom salt with 1 gallon of water.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Banana Peel Fertilizer: Bury banana peels around plants or dry and crush them for fertilizer tea.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Coffee Ground Fertilizer: Mix 1 part coffee grounds with 10 parts water for fertilizer tea.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Eggshell Calcium Fertilizer: Crush eggshells and mix into soil.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Bokashi Compost: Use vegetable scraps, sawdust, and microorganisms.
